data.title: Apollo Taps 13 Wall Street Banks for $9 Billion ADT Debt Package
data.description: According to Bloomberg, Apollo Global Management Inc. has enlisted 13 Wall Street lenders for a roughly $9 billion debt package it underwrote for Thrive Holdings Inc.’s acquisition of home security provider ADT Inc., according to people familiar with the matter.

data.title: OMERS Private Capital Head Michael Block to Become Teranet CEO
data.description: According to Bloomberg, Michael Block is leaving his role as head of private capital at the Ontario Municipal Employees Retirement System (OMERS) to become chief executive officer of Teranet Inc., one of OMERS’s infrastructure portfolio companies.

data.title: STOCKS | Canada Benchmark Heads for Longest Losing Streak Since 2023 Amid Tech Rout
data.description: According to Bloomberg, Canada’s major equities index is on track to fall for a seventh straight session after a broad selloff on Friday led by technology and commodities stocks. The streak would be the benchmark’s longest in three years.

data.title: Jensen Huang to Testify Publicly Before Senate Banking Panel, Tim Scott Says
data.description: According to CNBC, a spokesperson for Senate Banking Committee Chair Tim Scott said Friday that Jensen Huang will testify publicly before the panel. The date has not been announced; Scott initially requested that Huang appear on Dec. 3. Huang also agreed to a closed-door, transcribed interview with three House committees on Dec. 1.

data.title: U.S. Representatives Propose Anonymous Tip Line for Prediction Market Insider Trading
data.description: According to ChainCatcher, U.S. Representatives Sean Casten and Ted Lieu introduced a bill proposing an anonymous tip mechanism at the Department of Justice for reporting insider trading in prediction markets. Tipsters could receive rewards if their information leads to enforcement action.

data.title: Morgan Stanley Ends Anthropic Stock Support After One Day
data.description: Morgan Stanley ended its support arrangement for Anthropic shares one day after the company’s IPO, removing a potential source of market buying. The bank had up to 30 days to use the mechanism but closed it on Friday, as shares approached their $83 IPO price, according to BeInCrypto. Morgan Stanley bought all 147 million additional shares at $83 each through a greenshoe option, closing its short position tied to those shares. The purchase added $12.2 billion in gross proceeds for Anthropic, bringing the offering total to approximately $93.5 billion. Shares opened at $111.50 on Thursday, reached $115.10 and closed at $97.17 before falling as low as $83.93 in Friday premarket trading. The source said buyers near Thursday’s peak faced a roughly 27% loss. Berenberg analyst Carsten Hesse told Reuters that investors were losing “an important potential source of buying support.” A broader technology selloff added pressure, with $83 identified as the next major test; the support had never been guaranteed.

data.title: Trump Says He Retains Confidence in Lutnick
data.description: According to CNBC, President Donald Trump said Friday that he still has confidence in Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, pushing back on pressure from bipartisan lawmakers and members of his own administration.

data.title: BENQI Plans New Queue Mechanism to Shorten sAVAX Unstaking Wait Times
data.description: According to ChainCatcher citing The Defiant, Avalanche lending protocol BENQI plans to introduce a new unstaking queue for the liquid staking token sAVAX to reduce the time users wait to redeem AVAX. Under the proposal, pending unstaking requests will carry over to the new queue without resetting users’ time already spent waiting. Existing sAVAX holders will not need to migrate their positions or exchange tokens.

data.title: Emmanuel Moulin Says ECB Must Return Inflation to 2%
data.description: European Central Bank Governing Council member Emmanuel Moulin said policymakers still have work to do to restore price stability and bring inflation back to 2%, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: Transportation Department Watchdog to Review FAA Oversight of Boeing and Other Aircraft Makers
data.description: According to Jin10, the Transportation Department’s inspector general will review the Federal Aviation Administration’s oversight of Boeing (BA.N) and other aircraft manufacturers.

data.title: Trump Wants Jensen Huang to Apologize Before Returning to Lead Nvidia
data.description: According to Sina Finance, U.S. President Donald Trump said at a White House press conference that he wants Jensen Huang to apologize before returning to Nvidia. Trump said Nvidia should accept Huang’s apology and let him return if the company is wise.

data.title: AI | T. Rowe Price’s Emma Norchet Sees Anthropic Growth Beyond Coding
data.description:
Anthropic shares have retreated after their blockbuster debut, and T. Rowe Price participated in the IPO, according to Bloomberg. Emma Norchet, whose firm is one of Anthropic’s largest private investors, said the volatility hasn’t changed its long-term outlook.

Norchet cited improving compute economics and growth opportunities beyond coding, including knowledge work, cybersecurity, biology and robotics.

data.title: Anna Paulson Backs Deliberate Hikes to Bring Inflation to 2% Target
data.description: Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia President Anna Paulson favored a deliberate pace of interest-rate increases and said she would consider back-to-back moves at upcoming meetings to bring inflation to the central bank’s 2% target, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: AI | Morgan Stanley Sees Australian Dollar Outperforming in 2027
data.description: According to Bloomberg, Andrew Watrous at Morgan Stanley said the Australian dollar will stand out among developed-market currencies next year, benefiting from the artificial intelligence buildout and weathering the recent stock selloff.

data.title: Argentina Bonds Enter Distressed Territory for First Time in Two Years Amid Global Risk-Off
data.description: According to Bloomberg, Argentina’s debt slipped into distressed territory for the first time in two years as a global flight from risk deepened a bond selloff fueled by anxiety over next year’s election.
